results.title: 13 arrested over alleged impersonation, extortion at mining sites in Eastern and Western Regions
results.content: Thirteen people have been arrested in two separate operations in the Eastern and Western Regions for allegedly posing as state security operatives and demanding money from miners. The arrests followed intelligence reports that the suspects had been visiting mining sites while claiming to represent the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), National Security or other state institutions. In the first incident, six suspects were arrested at Twiapiase in the Eastern Region on November 18, 2026, after community members reported that a group had allegedly visited two suspected illegal mining sites and demanded money from miners. According to NAIMOS, the information was relayed to its task force at Kyebi, which moved to the area to verify the report.

results.title: Korle Bu sends five-year-old Miguel home for further tests, schedules review for November 24
results.content: Five-year-old Miguel Ntsiful, whose family has paid GH¢77,561 towards his brain tumour surgery at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital, is still awaiting the procedure after doctors requested further medical investigations during his latest visit. Miguel spent almost the entire day at the hospital on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, but was eventually asked to return home and undergo additional tests, including MRI scans of his brain and spine. His mother has been asked to bring him back on Tuesday, November 24, after completing the investigations. The latest development extends a wait that has lasted more than two months since the family paid the full amount raised for the operation directly into Korle Bu’s account on September 14. Following earlier reports on Miguel’s condition, the hospital asked his mother to bring him in on November 18 for further attention.

results.title: “We can’t even make light soup” – Bryan Acheampong says Nkoko Nkitinkiti has failed
results.content: Former Agriculture Minister Bryan Acheampong has criticised the government’s flagship Nkoko Nkitinkiti poultry programme, saying its output after two years is too small to make a meaningful contribution to Ghana’s chicken consumption. “You promised us Nkoko Nkitinkiti, and within two years you have not been able to deliver even 2%. We can't even make light soup with the Nkoko Nkitinkiti you have produced,” the Abetifi MP said during the parliamentary debate on the 2027 Budget. He claimed the programme had delivered fewer than three million birds in two years, representing less than one per cent of Ghana’s estimated annual poultry demand of 350 million birds. “This is your flagship programme. results.title: Ghana Prisons Service reports improved inmate meals after feeding allowance rises to GH¢5
results.content: The Ghana Prisons Service says the increase in the daily feeding allowance for inmates from GH¢1.80 to GH¢5 has led to improvements in the quality and nutritional value of meals served in prisons across the Ashanti Region. The Service’s Ashanti Regional Public Relations Officer, Chief Superintendent Richard Bukari, described the adjustment as a significant relief, saying it has enabled prison authorities to provide inmates with more protein and other nutritional additions. Speaking to JoyNews, he said inmates at facilities including Kumasi Central Prison now receive eggs up to three times a week, while more fish is added to their meals. “I can tell you that we are able to give the inmates egg three times in a week. results.title: University of Ghana admits concerns over UGEL hostel conditions, says phased renovations underway
results.content: The University of Ghana has acknowledged concerns about the condition of some residential facilities managed by the University of Ghana Enterprise Limited (UGEL), saying renovation works have started and will be carried out in phases. In a statement signed by Registrar Michael Opare Atuah, management said it took complaints about sanitation, maintenance and other deficiencies seriously, stressing that students deserved safe, decent and well-maintained accommodation. “Plans are in place and renovation has already started; this is being done in phases,” the statement said. The university explained that major rehabilitation works were traditionally undertaken during the long vacation, when the halls were largely unoccupied. However, it said recent changes to the academic calendar had shortened vacation periods, reducing the time available for extensive maintenance and construction.

results.title: KNUST teams win top honours at 2026 Next Generation Digital Action programme in Denmark
results.content: A team of students from the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) has won the Meteorological Innovation Challenge at the 2026 Next Generation Digital Action (NGDA) programme in Copenhagen, Denmark. The team, comprising Richard Kofi Doh, Kelvin Kojo Adoboe and Joana Abrafi Addo, secured the Challenge Winner Award and a €1,000 accelerator prize for developing a digital solution to improve the flow of meteorological information in Ghana. The team was also named Ghana's Best National Team in the Young Academics competition, following its performance against university teams from Tanzania, Egypt and Denmark.
